- The timeline (delay of weeks after trauma) and the presence of a cataract with clumps of material over the lens and extruding into anterior vitreous are highly suggestive of lens material provoking inflammation. Two lens‑related syndromes fit: (1) phacoantigenic (phacogenic) uveitis—granulomatous inflammation to exposed lens proteins after capsule rupture—and (2) lens‑particle induced inflammation (and possible secondary phacolytic phenomena). Both can present weeks after trauma with fibrinous AC reaction, cyclitic membranes, iris changes and severe vision loss.
